scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the FRR BGP control-plane on leaf_router_0_0 (bgpd within the frr service) is down.

Mechanism: With bgpd stopped on the leaf, both BGP sessions to the spines drop simultaneously even though the L3 uplink interfaces remain UP. The leaf therefore has only connected routes and no fabric routes. Traffic from pc_0_0 to remote subnet 10.0.1.0/24 is forwarded to the leaf’s gateway (10.0.0.1), which immediately returns ICMP “Destination Net Unreachable” because it has no route to that network.

Localization: leaf_router_0_0. Interfaces eth0 (172.16.0.5/31 to spine_router_0_0) and eth1 (172.16.0.9/31 to spine_router_0_1) are UP (confirmed in ip addr). However, bgpd is not running on the device: “show bgp summary” returns “bgpd is not running,” and systemctl reports “frr.service … Active: inactive (dead).” On both spines, the BGP neighbors 172.16.0.5 and 172.16.0.9 are in “Active,” corroborating the down state on the leaf. The leaf’s routing table contains only connected routes (no route to 10.0.1.0/24), and pc_0_0→pc_0_1 pings show “From 10.0.0.1 Destination Net Unreachable,” proving the leaf generated the error.

Root cause: The FRR service (bgpd) on leaf_router_0_0 is stopped/inactive, causing loss of BGP peering to both spines and loss of fabric reachability.

Corrective fix: Start and enable FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (e.g., systemctl start frr; systemctl enable frr). Verify “show bgp summary” shows Established to both spines and that routes (e.g., 10.0.1.0/24) are installed. Confirm pc_0_0 can reach 10.0.1.2. Review logs (journalctl -u frr and /var/log/frr/*) to determine why the service stopped and prevent recurrence.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the fault to leaf_router_0_0 in both the affected-component and localization fields.
The agent explicitly states that bgpd (the FRR BGP daemon) on leaf_router_0_0 is stopped/inactive and that BGP sessions are down.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis does not state that the spines, super-spine, or leaf_router_0_1 are healthy or that their other BGP sessions remain Established; it only focuses on the down leaf and its neighbor state.
Proposes starting/enabling the FRR service on leaf_router_0_0 (systemctl start/enable and verification), which will restore bgpd and re-establish the BGP sessions as required.

The agent's findings are directly supported by logs showing bgpd is not running, the frr service is inactive, and pings return ICMP Destination Net Unreachable from the leaf; the causal chain (bgpd down → BGP sessions drop → loss of fabric routes → unreachable remote subnet) is sound. Minor claims (leaf routing table containing only connected routes; explicit 'Active' state on spines) are plausible but not fully shown in the truncated log, so grounding and coverage are rated slightly below perfect.
